Hi Sam —

Quick technical breakdown of how Redwood bills streaming responses and how we handle disconnects/retries. TL;DR: we bill for committed/generated tokens that the runtime has accepted as output; we have resume/dedupe behavior within a short resume window to prevent double billing for stitch/resume.

Details (examples use your numbers):
- Runtime behavior: our serving runtime emits token chunks over the stream as they are produced. For billing we consider a token "committed" when it reaches the runtime's send buffer and is acknowledged by the downstream transport layer. Practically this means tokens that were actually transmitted by the server before the TCP connection dropped are counted.
- Interrupted streams: in your case where ~320 tokens were transmitted before the disconnect, those 320 tokens are billed. We do not automatically charge the full requested length (1500) unless the model finished generation and returned a finalization marker.
- Resume/dedup window: when a client reconnects using the same session id within our resume window (default 60s, configurable per-customer up to 120s), the runtime attempts to stitch the prior partial output to avoid re-generating already-emitted tokens. When stitch succeeds, we suppress duplicate token generation and you are not double-billed. If the stitch fails (e.g., missing KV cache), the runtime may re-generate some tokens — in that case the new tokens are billed, but we flag the session for review.
- Retries and idempotency: for client-side retries that re-send the same request body with the same request id, our gateway will recognise the idempotent intent and avoid duplicating charges for work already completed. If a retry results in an overlapping but not identical request (e.g., different temperature/params), those tokens are billed.

Numeric example based on your report:
- You requested 1500 tokens. 320 tokens were emitted and transmitted, then connection dropped. You reconnected within 40s and resumed; reconnect stitch succeeded. Billed tokens: ~320.
- If stitch had failed and the service re-generated 300 tokens to reach the same point, billed tokens would be ~620 (the original 320 + the 300 new).

What we can do for audits/credits:
- We will review the session id/logs you attached. If we find an instance where our system re-generated tokens due to an internal fault (not client-side mismatch), we’ll issue a one-time credit for the duplicated tokens.
- For pilot customers we typically have a grace policy: first 3 incidents related to interrupted streams where stitch/dedupe should have prevented double-work are eligible for credit without requiring escalation.

If you can confirm the session id (from the log) and the two timestamps (client disconnect and reconnect), I’ll run the trace and report back with the exact billed token count and any recommended credits.

Regards,
